clue.text: Metal from beasts wild and woolly

parts.note: the wild one of the two beasts is a wolf, a wild canine predator
the woolly one of the two beasts is a ram, a male sheep with a fleece

explanation.surface: A metal apparently extracted from rough, shaggy animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beasts' covers both pieces: one wild beast, one woolly beast. Wolfram is the old name for tungsten.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a heavy metallic element.

clue.text: Deer seen in an excavation in Mayfair

indicators.note: seen in places the hole dug out inside the London district

parts.note: Mayfair is in the London postal district W1, written here as WI
a pit is a hole dug out

explanation.surface: A stag spotted in a hole dug in a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an upmarket area of central London with the postcode W1.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the large North American elk.

clue.text: Pupil on strike is hard, rough and uncouth

parts.note: L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
workers on strike are out
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A schoolchild taking industrial action is tough, crude and ill-mannered.
explanation.definitionFit: Loutish behaviour is coarse and boorish, like that of a lout.

clue.text: Air of fragrance or colour once embracing the French style

parts.note: red is a colour

indicators.note: embracing means the word once wraps round the French article

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Some scent or old shade taking on a Gallic flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps ONCE round the French article to make OLENCE. 'style' fills out the surface and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolence is a pleasant smell or scent, the quality of being sweet-smelling.

clue.text: Sweet product of the wet land, many admit

parts.note: a marsh is boggy ground
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, taken as many
to allow is to let in or admit

explanation.surface: A confection made from swamp produce, as most people concede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product of the' links the sweet to the marsh plant it was once made from.
explanation.definitionFit: The marshmallow is a soft spongy confection originally made from the root of a marsh plant.

clue.text: For whom a headline may help to make a fortune?

definitions.text: For whom a headline may help to make a fortune?

parts.words: For whom a headline may help to make a fortune
parts.note: the head line is one of the creases on the hand, read by someone who tells a fortune, not a newspaper banner that makes someone rich

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline helps someone get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller who reads hands studies the head line among other creases of the palm.

clue.text: Lodging for an old-time horse

definitions.meaning: slang for one's flat or place to stay
an archaic word for an easy-paced riding horse

explanation.surface: A stable for a horse of bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is slang for a home or flat, and an old word for a road horse with an easy gait.

clue.text: Sign for much of the book collection

indicators.note: much of means most but not all of the word, so its end is dropped

parts.note: a library is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A notice for most of the books in a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Get in trouble about coming up with a figure

indicators.note: trouble shows the letters of get in are thrown into disorder
coming up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: re means about

explanation.surface: Get into difficulty over arriving with a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns GET IN into INTEG; 'coming up' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, a numerical figure without fractions.

clue.text: Reaction of Hoffmann's Augustus to the soup from this restaurant?

definitions.text: Reaction of Hoffmann's Augustus to the soup from this restaurant?

parts.words: Reaction of Hoffmann's Augustus to the soup from this restaurant
parts.note: in Heinrich Hoffmann's Struwwelpeter, Augustus refuses his soup, so his reaction would be to have it removed; also a shop selling food to eat elsewhere

explanation.surface: How a picky boy from a German storybook responds to this eatery's soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus in Struwwelpeter cries 'I won't have any soup today!' and wastes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeaway is a shop selling cooked food to be eaten off the premises.

clue.text: One's out of place under news chief, getting sacked

indicators.note: one thing being out of another means it is taken away from that word

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
taken as written
ED, short for editor, the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone displaced beneath a newspaper boss ends up fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes ACE from PLACE, leaving PL. 'sacked' is the definition in its sense of looted, not fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A city that was sacked has been looted and pillaged by invaders.

clue.text: Printed material brought together in a small book

annotationWithheld.why: Printed material brought together in a small book (5): the clue is as printed; B..K (a small book) around A gives BA_K, but no reading of 'brought together' gives TI, so the parse is unknown
annotationWithheld.clue: Printed material brought together in a small book

clue.text: Hearing noisy neighbour could be one

definitions.meaning: a hearing in court, where a case is tried
a source of annoyance or hardship, something that tests patience

explanation.surface: A court hearing about a noisy neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is both a court case and a burden or nuisance one has to put up with.

clue.text: Flowering shrub to give cover to forest officer, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to give cover to is to hide; a forest officer is a ranger

explanation.surface: A bush used to shelter a woodland warden.
explanation.walkthrough: HIDE RANGER spoken quickly sounds like the shrub's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a garden bush with large rounded heads of blossom.

clue.text: Show way to chide the devil on top

indicators.note: on top puts the devil first, above the rest in a down entry

parts.note: a demon is a devil
ST, short for street, a way
to rate is an old verb for to scold

explanation.surface: Display how to scold Satan from above.
explanation.walkthrough: To rate someone is an old-fashioned way of saying to scold them. 'on top' means the devil comes first in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is to exhibit or prove by display.

clue.text: Thomas, gets par again extraordinary show of illusion

indicators.note: extraordinary describes the letters of the three words as being in an unusual, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A golfer called Thomas scores par yet again, an amazing display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' looks like part of the definition but signals the anagram; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantasmagoria was a Victorian magic-lantern display of ghostly images, hence any shifting dreamlike spectacle.

clue.text: Such exercises ruined my casting

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of my casting are wrecked and put back in another order

explanation.surface: Those workouts spoiled my selection for the role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such exercises' stands for the adjective: gymnastic exercises are exercises of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnastic describes athletic training such as vaulting, tumbling and bar work.

clue.text: Spray given first of all to Scrooge

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
Ebenezer Scrooge, Dickens's tight-fisted character, is a byword for a miser

explanation.surface: A squirt aimed first and foremost at a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns a liquid such as perfume into a fine spray.

clue.text: Those detailed by Mrs Giles

parts.note: detailed means had their tails removed; Mrs Giles stands for the farmer's wife of the nursery rhyme, who cut off the tails of three sightless rodents with a carving knife

explanation.surface: People itemised in a report by a woman named Giles.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer Giles is a stock British name for a farmer, so Mrs Giles is the farmer's wife of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, the farmer's wife cuts off the tails of the three sightless rodents.

clue.text: A very fine type of snake

definitions.meaning: old slang for an excellent example of something, a first-rate one
a rattlesnake, by its informal shortened name

explanation.surface: An excellent kind of serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is colloquial for something first-rate and also short for rattlesnake.

clue.text: Elegance given a trial in Illinois

parts.note: chic means style or elegance
a go is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: Style tested out in a Midwestern state.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the largest city of the US state of Illinois.

clue.text: Some swimmers take this breather during physical education

indicators.note: during places the breather inside the school subject

parts.note: PE, the school subject
a lung is an organ one breathes with

explanation.surface: Swimmers pause for breath during a school games lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest but is the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunge is a dive into water, which swimmers take from the side.

clue.text: In this forum other witnesses show common sense

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a public forum, other witnesses display good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother wit is native shrewdness, the practical sense one is born with.

clue.text: Hoped for a change of vestment

indicators.note: for a change means the letters of hoped are switched around

explanation.surface: A wish for a new set of robes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephod is a linen garment worn by ancient Jewish priests.

clue.text: One in real trouble freed by the Duke of Milan

definitions.text: freed by the Duke of Milan

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
trouble suggests the letters of real are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in difficulty is released by an Italian nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes AREL from REAL. In Shakespeare's The Tempest, Prospero, the rightful Duke of Milan, frees the spirit Ariel at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Tempest the airy spirit serving Prospero, the Duke of Milan, is released by him.

clue.text: She shows originally slender young lines -perfectly heavenly

indicators.note: originally means taking what comes at the start of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A woman displays a slim youthful figure, simply divine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is a slender graceful girl, or an elemental spirit of the air.

clue.text: Clever chap swallows a tot perhaps going to Dover in this

indicators.note: swallows means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a brain is a clever person

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of a tot are to be taken in some other order

explanation.surface: A bright fellow downs a small drink, maybe on the way to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes OATT from A TOT. Dover is the English port where ferries leave for France.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat train ran from London to meet the cross-Channel ferries at ports such as Dover.

clue.text: A kiss, say, which may transport one

indicators.note: say signals a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an old word for a kiss

explanation.surface: A peck on the cheek that could carry someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a public vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Concerning duplicated functions of the screen

indicators.note: duplicated means the word for concerning is used twice over

parts.note: re means about or concerning
dos are parties or social functions

explanation.surface: About repeated duties of a display panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental partition behind a church altar.

clue.text: Bound to finish, following directions

indicators.note: following places the word for finish after the directions

parts.note: E and N, the compass points east and north
a close is an end or finish

explanation.surface: Certain to end up obeying instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it is a verb meaning to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound an area is to form its limits, to surround it.
